title: Emphasis and fronting
tagline: Stress the right word, front the right phrase, and a plain statement becomes unmistakable.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations (DID, DOES, THIS, UTTERLY, OWN)
Writing Part 1 — essay: making a point stand out without shouting it
Speaking Parts 3 and 4 — sounding convincing, not just correct
Listening — recognising stress and contradiction in spoken English
why: At C1, emphasis is not just about intonation — English has grammatical tools that do the stressing for you: emphatic do, fronting, intensifying adverbs and fixed phrases like the thing is. Use of English Part 4 tests several of these directly, and a well-placed one lifts an essay or a spoken answer out of the merely correct.

diagrams.title: Emphatic do / does / did
diagrams.caption: Do/does/did carries the stress that a plain past or present tense doesn't have.

diagrams.title: Normal order vs. fronting for emphasis

rows.label: Adverbial fronting
cells: The results were disappointing, to say the least.
To say the least, the results were disappointing.

rows.label: Negative object fronting
cells: She didn't say a single word.
Not a single word did she say.

rows.label: Effect
cells: The fronted element carries the stress

head: Pattern
Structure
Example
rows: I did warn you about the traffic.
This I can accept; the rest I cannot.
Not a word did she say for the rest of the journey.
She wrote the whole script in her own words.
The very idea of cheating disgusted him.
the thing is, for emphasis in speech
The thing is, we simply ran out of time.

use.point: Emphatic do/does/did to stress that something really happened

examples.text: I did send the report — check your spam folder.
She does care about the result, even if she hides it.
We did try to warn them, but nobody listened.

use.point: Fronting an object, adverbial or negative expression for emphasis

examples.text: This I can accept; the deadline extension, I cannot.
To say the least, the meeting did not go as planned.
Not a single word did she say for the rest of the journey.

use.point: Intensifying adverbs with the right collocation

examples.text: The behaviour was utterly unacceptable in a school assembly.
His comment was downright rude, whatever his intention.
She seemed thoroughly convinced by the argument.

use.point: own, very and the thing is for emphasis without raising your voice

examples.text: He insisted on writing the speech in his own words, not a template.
The very mention of exams made the room go quiet.
The thing is, we can't reschedule without losing the deposit.

watch_out.wrong: I do sent the report yesterday.
watch_out.why: Emphatic do/does/did is followed by the bare infinitive, never a past tense form.
After a fronted object, the clause keeps normal, non-inverted word order — no extra to.

watch_out.wrong: Not a single word she said.
watch_out.right: Not a single word did she say.
watch_out.why: Fronting a negative object triggers subject-auxiliary inversion.

watch_out.wrong: The excuse was very unconvincing, downright.
watch_out.why: Downright/utterly/thoroughly go immediately before the adjective, not after it.

watch_out.wrong: The very of exams made her nervous.
watch_out.right: The very mention of exams made her nervous.
watch_out.why: Very must be followed by a noun in this pattern — it cannot stand alone.
The fixed phrase needs the definite article and a comma before the explanation.

dialogue.title: Who did the reading
dialogue.context: Mateo, Liam and Miss Vega sort out a disagreement about a group project, with tempers running high enough for some real emphasis.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: The group project mark was much lower than everyone expected. What happened?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: I did do my part, Miss — I sent Liam my notes on Monday.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: This I have to say: I never received any notes from anyone.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: I did send them! Check your email, not just WhatsApp.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Let's stay calm. Liam, what exactly is missing?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: The thing is, the whole introduction was left half-finished.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: That's because Sofia said she'd write it — whatever she wrote, it never reached me.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Right. And how would you describe the final result, honestly?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Utterly disorganised, if I'm honest. Nobody checked the final draft.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: I agree it was downright messy — but I really did try to keep it together.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good. Whoever is missing something, next time everyone confirms their part in writing.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Not a single message will I send without a screenshot from now on.

items.sentence: I ___ send the invitation — check your inbox again.
items.why: Emphatic did + bare infinitive stresses a past action, contradicting doubt.

items.sentence: She ___ care about the outcome, whatever she says.
items.why: Present simple emphatic uses does + bare infinitive.

items.sentence: ___ I can accept, but the extra cost is out of the question.
items.why: Fronting the object (This) throws stress onto what follows, contrasting it with what can't be accepted.

items.sentence: Not a single excuse ___ willing to accept.
items.why: Fronting a negative object triggers subject-auxiliary inversion.

items.sentence: The comment was ___ inappropriate for a school assembly.
items.why: Utterly is an intensifying adverb placed directly before the adjective.

items.sentence: He always insists on doing it in his ___ way.
items.why: Own after a possessive emphasises that nobody else is involved.

items.sentence: ___, we simply don't have the budget for a second trip.
items.why: The fixed phrase the thing is introduces the real issue behind a decision.

summary: Emphatic do/does/did + bare infinitive stresses that something really did happen — useful for contradicting doubt.
Fronting an object, adverbial or negative expression throws stress onto it; a fronted negative also triggers inversion.
Intensifying adverbs like utterly, downright, thoroughly collocate with specific adjectives — learn them as pairs.
own, the very and the thing is add emphasis without raising your voice; whatever/whoever add emphatic indifference.
These devices work because they are used sparingly — save them for the moment that really needs the stress.
